source_reconciliation.statement: Current proof routes use verified free editions and complete independently written arguments. Historical attribution is distinguished from original-proof reading. An exhaustive literature survey is not claimed.
source_reconciliation.remaining_proof_limit: The scalar and reverse Bott–Dirac products used by the selected KK descent route are supplied by KT-KK-12, Lemma 4.0, Theorems 4.1 and 5.2, Propositions 7.1–7.2 and Theorem 7.3. KT-OPK-21 Proposition 6.3 and KT-OPK-23 Corollary 6.5 retain their separability and countability hypotheses. This correspondence does not certify every transitive dependency of either course.

consumers.conditions: Separable possibly nonunital A, automorphism alpha, translation action on its mapping torus; even Green Morita classes. In degree i the inverse map is (-1)^i times the ordinary Wiener–Hopf comparison.
Finite-rank free group acting on a separable possibly nonunital coefficient algebra; both full/reduced coefficient products retained.

proof_provider_routes.scalar_foundation: KT-KK-12 Lemma 4.0, Theorems 4.1 and 5.2, Propositions 7.1–7.2 and Theorem 7.3; used by KT-KK-18 Lemma 5.1.
proof_provider_routes.scope: Exact provider correspondence for the named consumers; no whole-course or unrestricted-source proof claim.

consumers.conditions: Irrational real parameter; full finite projective modules over a unital rotation algebra. The A_(1/t)-A_t module has right trace dimension t for positive t, and its K-map goes from left to right; inversion reverses the scale. Small positive dimensions use primitive integer pairs and the full GL2(Z) construction.
Irrational real parameters and the full GL2(Z) orbit, not only determinant +1 or the unital-isomorphism orbit.

consumers.result: KT-OPK-23 Section 2, full AF corner stabilization
consumers.conditions: Both algebras sigma-unital; satisfied by the proved full corner and separability. Both stabilization tensor factors retained.

hilbert_module_proof_provider_routes.acyclicity: The torus provider uses KT-OPK-20 Theorems 2.1, 3.1 and 5.1, not its cancellation Theorem 5.2.

consumers.conditions: Bounded trace, unnormalized matrix trace, scalar-zero linear extension for relative K0; the consumer supplies its own proof.

Arbitrary Hilbert spaces and rectangular trace-class operators; bounded multipliers and finite-rank trace-norm approximation. Only the prescribed integer powers of parametrix errors need be trace class.

Norm-dense derivation and bounded invariant trace produce a dense antisymmetric dual-valued derivation. Use its norm-closed graph domain, not an assumed inverse-closed initial domain. Retain matrix amplification, relative unitization and 1/(2 pi i) normalization.

cyclic_analytic_proof_provider_routes.scope: The named proofs and their immediate inverse-closure and approximation arguments were read against these consumer uses. Public reader formulas, text and anchors agree with the checked private versions. Other portions of the provider lessons and transitive prerequisites are not certified by this reconciliation.
cyclic_analytic_proof_provider_routes.download_scope: These proof routes require online access; the course download does not embed the provider lessons.

consumers.conditions: Arbitrary C*-weight finite domains and GNS, including zero and nonunital algebras; null quotient before completion; linear-first inner product. Two-sidedness and cyclicity are proved separately under the trace hypothesis.

No countability or prior fullness assumption. The consumer checks all four axioms and its everywhere-defined antiunitary involution. Only that tracial case turns the constructed faithful normal semifinite weight into a trace; the original coefficient trace may be nonfaithful.

Actual closed measurable operators for a faithful normal semifinite trace; arbitrary Hilbert spaces, arbitrary finite-projection nets, possibly infinite identity trace; completeness, bounded multiplication, L2 products in L1 and cyclicity. The infinite coefficient action retains its additional graph-norm continuity hypothesis (6.0).
P,Q orthogonal; P-Q compact; (P-Q)^(2j+1) trace class, integer j>=0. Index of QP:PH to QH has the positive trace sign. This is not used in the independent Calderon-Fedosov proof.

topological_character_foundations.additions: Exact singular-chain, excision, product, Thom/Euler and projective/flag providers; explicit sign translation and bounded cohomology along flag towers; explicit CW homotopy-extension retraction and corrected stable gluing homotopy.
topological_character_foundations.scope: Cohomological projective basis retained and extended via its full Hausdorff-base provider; actual splitting specifies paracompact Hausdorff bases. Rational character still has its finite CW scope. Integral K-projective theorem retains every compact Hausdorff base and both degrees.
topological_character_foundations.preservation: Both Whitney approaches, hyperplane and Gysin projective calculations, Bott and both boundary signs, graded products, full assigned statements, anchors and all five solutions remain.
topological_character_foundations.not_certified: Finite direct-provider reconciliation, not independent review, recursive foundational closure or whole-course completion. Three external programme readers remain online dependencies of the download.

finite_cw_total_space_proof.result: The total projective bundle and each finite flag tower over a compact Hausdorff base of finite CW homotopy type have finite CW homotopy type.
finite_cw_total_space_proof.argument: Cylinder attachments, homotopic attaching maps and replacement by a homotopy-equivalent preceding space; explicit collar homeomorphism; cellular approximation and finite relative product cells; canonical pullback total-space maps proved homotopy equivalences by cylinder transport.
finite_cw_total_space_proof.scope: Closes the previously recorded finite-CW-model assertion. It does not certify recursive closure of every other prerequisite or independent review; existing proofs and broader projective-bundle scope are preserved.

mapping_torus_proof_provider_routes.scope: Exact Green, Morita, Thom, scalar Bott and boundary-normalization routes; all existing statements, proofs, hypotheses and solutions retained. Public-reader availability is not recursive proof certification or independent review.
mapping_torus_proof_provider_routes.hypotheses: The ordinary K-group comparison retains arbitrary, possibly nonunital C*-algebras. The KK comparison requires separable coefficients and countably generated modules; no nonseparable KK claim is added.
mapping_torus_proof_provider_routes.normalization: Induced covariance f(t+n)=alpha^(-n)(f(t)); F(t)=f(-t); tau_r F(t)=F(t+r). The inverse real Thom class is minus the dual Thom class followed by Takai Morita. Its conjugate-Green composite on K_i is (-1)^i times the ordinary boundary comparison.
mapping_torus_proof_provider_routes.remaining: Other proof chains and the separate KK18 K-amenability routes are not certified by this repair. The download links to online programme prerequisites.

kamenability_proof_provider_routes.consumer: KT-OPK-23 Corollary 6.5 and the following free-product permanence paragraph
kamenability_proof_provider_routes.scope: Exact coefficient quotient, rooted-tree cycle, descent and reduced-norm proof routes; all earlier statements and proofs retained. The coefficient KK claim assumes separability; the separate elementary coefficient K-theory sequence retains arbitrary coefficients.
kamenability_proof_provider_routes.generality: The linked provider proves the quotient KK-equivalence for every separable graded algebra acted on by a second-countable locally compact K-amenable group, tree K-amenability for countable trees without inversions with amenable stabilizers, and finite or countable free-product permanence for countable discrete K-amenable factors. The stated finite-rank free-group corollary is not substituted for those full results.
kamenability_proof_provider_routes.remaining: This is a checked immediate proof dependency, not independent review or recursive certification of all foundations. The download uses online prerequisite readers; other lesson dependencies keep their existing status.

compact_duality_and_averaging_routes.consumer: KT-OPK23 Section2 and Section6 word averaging; exact current proof dependencies.
compact_duality_and_averaging_routes.scope: Haar-corner isomorphism is not automatic fullness; preserve the consumer saturation argument. Check maximal tensor norms before passing the inactive compact factor, the positive dual convention and its inverse stage shift. Retain the all-finite-rank free-group argument, not only the two-generator provider.
compact_duality_and_averaging_routes.remaining: Direct dependencies read and self-checked, not independent review or recursive certification of every analytic foundation. Programme proof prerequisites remain online for the download.

canonical_scope_reconciliation.norm_lift: Corollary 2.4 needs a contraction lift, including the zero quotient; no nonzero-quotient hypothesis is added. The partial-isometry construction and all conclusions are unchanged.
